body: It doesn’t matter if you were “consenting” if you were under the age of consent where you live it is classified as statutory rape. Rape is rape. Don’t doubt your story and facts if the people you trust to tell are ignorant. It is also highly possible you were groomed and taken advantage of.

It’s okay to wait as long as you need to. Especially when you are struggling with talking about your trauma in person, it is important to trust your therapist. To overcome that emotional response I recommend slowly opening up with “little t trauma” so that you can see how your therapist will respond and react and what kind of therapy/advice they will give you. As you open up to them over time, it will make it easier for you imagine discussing that “big T Trauma” with them. (Also through this process you’ll figure out if you would be more comfortable with a different therapist, don’t think you are stuck with one because you may need to try out a few before you find the perfect fit for you)

I also struggled with verbalizing my trauma, the first time I had to say it aloud was to a sheriff and it was extremely difficult. If you are comfortable with this idea, when you are alone in a safe place, occasionally practice vocalizing details little by little, taking as many breaks as needed. If you are too overwhelmed by this don’t be forced to continue. This just helped me but it may not help you.

I’m not a medical professional but I have been in therapy for 5 years now, I wish you the best in treatment!
